claim.summary: Published (Turan 1984, Theorem 33.3): for f = 1 + sum a_n n^-s with |f| >= log^-10(3+|t|) for sigma > 1, meromorphic in sigma >= 1/2 with |f| <= |t|^(A1(1-sigma)) log^10|t| (read on 1/2 <= sigma <= 1), and f'/f = sum b_n n^-s with |b_n| <= c log n: if |sum over N1 <= n <= N2 of b_n e^(-i tau0 log n)| < c N log^100 N / |tau0|^A3 for all tau0^A2 <= N <= N1 < N2 <= 2N, then f has no zero on sigma > 1 - A4, t = tau0, where A4 is the greatest x with x log(A3/(A1 x)) <= A3^2/(300 A1 A2), x <= (A3/(4 A2)) exp(-(4 A2 + A3)/A2), x <= 9 A3/(1000 A1), x <= A3/(1600 A2).
claim.assessment: Statement and proof read as page images from a supplied scan; not audited, and some exponents are uncertain readings. The proof compares a high derivative of f'/f at 1 + mu + i tau0 computed from the Dirichlet series (using the hypothesis) with its expression through the zeros in a disk of radius 8 mu, and applies Turan's second main theorem to that power sum; the number of zeros in the disk is bounded by Jensen's formula. With A2 >= A3 the last constraint gives A4 <= 1/1600 for every pair of exponents: the linear constraints come from choosing mu tiny, and the first from the power-sum loss over the Jensen count.

significance.rationale: The one read implication from a bound on prime exponential sums at one height to the absence of a zero at that height; locating its two losses states the second half of the missing implication as an inequality to prove.
significance.next_action: Redo the proof under a hypothesis on the number of zeros in the disk, tracking constants; read the later sections for stronger forms and the converse theorem.

relationships.note: Its proof uses the second main theorem, whose loss the notebook's power-sum bounds also meet.

claim.summary: For complex z_1..z_N with |z_j| >= 1 (not necessarily distinct), complex b_j, s_nu = sum b_j z_j^nu and m >= 0: the maximum of |s_nu| over m < nu <= m + N is at least |b_1 + ... + b_N| / A(m,N), A(m,N) = sum over k < N of binom(m+k,k) 2^k <= 2^(N-1) binom(m+N, N-1), and A <= (2e(m+N)/N)^N for m >= N-1.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof by Newton interpolation of z^-(m+1), with divided differences expressed through complete homogeneous polynomials. Recalled by a reviewer as Turan's first main theorem with a later constant; neither read. For a cluster of n off-axis pairs it gives |S(s)| >= 2M e^{-delta_1 s}/A at one of 2n consecutive lattice points, with the exponential of the wrong sign, so in the goal's parameter it is below the trivial size and detects nothing.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Settles that the few-line gap-free route does not substitute for a bound normalized by the largest modulus, and records the conversion: a loss c^(2n) is below the gain only for clusters under a small multiple of log T pairs.
significance.next_action: Pass from a lattice point to the mean square for the interpolation bound; restate with Turan's second main theorem when its statement is available.
